title: Groundnut Soup with Chicken and Crushed Peanuts
summary: A rich West African peanut soup: bone-in chicken simmered in a tomato and peanut butter broth with ginger, garlic and a whole Scotch bonnet, topped with crushed peanuts.

ingredients.item: bone-in chicken drumsticks and thighs, skin removed
fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Season the chicken
steps.text: Rub the chicken with the ginger, garlic and 0.5 tsp salt and leave 20 min (or overnight in the fridge).

steps.title: Sear
steps.text: Heat the oil in the pot over medium-high heat and brown the chicken on both sides, about 6 min, in batches if needed. Lift out.

steps.title: Make the base
steps.text: Lower the heat, add the onion and cook 5 min until soft. Stir in the tomato paste for 2 min until it darkens, then add the blended tomatoes and cook 10 min until thick.

steps.title: Loosen the peanut butter
steps.text: Whisk the peanut butter in the bowl with 300 ml of the hot water until smooth, then stir it into the pot with the rest of the water.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Return the chicken, add the Scotch bonnet, bring to a simmer and cook partly covered for 40 min, stirring often so it does not catch, until the chicken is tender (75 °C at the bone) and red oil pools on top.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Remove the Scotch bonnet, add the remaining salt and taste. Thin with a little hot water if it is thicker than heavy cream.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve in bowls with crushed peanuts scattered over, with rice balls (omo tuo), fufu or plain rice.

tips: Stir often once the peanut butter is in; it catches easily on the bottom.
Red oil rising to the top is the sign that the soup is ready.
Leave the Scotch bonnet whole for warmth without too much heat.
storage: Keep in the fridge for up to 3 days or freeze for up to 3 months. It thickens as it stands; loosen with hot water when reheating. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
